A reading recipe as an arm of a benchmark

Source: R/doc-bench-arm.R
gr_arm.Rd

gr_arm() wraps one recipe as an hr_arm(), so recipes can be compared with hr_benchmark() on a reference of questions about documents, such as one from gr_qa_reference(). gr_arms() builds one arm per recipe.

Usage

gr_arm(recipe, settings = list(), name = NULL)

gr_arms(recipes, settings = list())

Arguments

recipe

A recipe: a name from gr_recipes(), "auto", a reader name, a gr_recipe() or a named list of ingest, segment and read.

settings

A named list of overrides applied to the recipe, as the ... of answer_document() takes them (for example model, top_k, max_tokens). An unknown name is an error when the arm is built.

name

The arm's name. By default the recipe's name.

recipes

A character vector of recipe names, or a list of recipes. The names of a named list or vector are used as the arms' names.

Value

gr_arm() returns an hr_arm(). gr_arms() returns a list of them, named by arm.

Details

Each run reads the item's document and answers its question: with answer_document() when the document is a file path, a web address or text, or with gr_read() when it is already cut into chunks by gr_segment(). It returns the gr_answer, which the benchmark's scorer then judges; gr_scorer_answer() is the scorer made for it.

The run uses the benchmark's client and records every request into the trace the benchmark made for that run (ctx$trace), so the run's tokens, cost and refusals are counted and held to the benchmark's limits, and the answer's trace is that run's trace. That trace also gives every request of the run the run's draw index (see draw_index in gr_call()), segmenter and reader requests included, so the runs of one arm on one item are separate draws under a gr_cache() or a gr_replay_client() rather than one stored reply repeated, which hr_benchmark() would refuse.

A reader checks before it starts whether the run's call and spending limits leave room for it. When they do not, the run returns a "NOT_IN_DOCUMENT" answer marked partial, with call_cap_reached or cost_cap_reached in its notes as gr_compare() records them, and gr_scorer_answer() scores it as a "budget_stop".

A recipe given as "auto" chooses "fast" or "thorough" per document, as answer_document() does; it needs a document that is not yet chunked.

The arm's params are the recipe's name and the settings, and its version is the version of harnessr, since readers and prompts change between versions.

See also

gr_qa_reference(), gr_scorer_answer(), hr_benchmark(), hr_report(), gr_compare() for a single descriptive comparison

Other harness: gr_qa_reference(), gr_scorer_answer(), hr_arm(), hr_benchmark(), hr_contrast(), hr_drift_check(), hr_mdd(), hr_reference(), hr_report(), hr_scorer()

Examples

cl <- gr_mock_client(function(m, p) "Revenue was 45.2 million dollars.")
ref <- gr_qa_reference(
  questions = c(revenue = "What was revenue in 2024?",
                ceo = "Who is the chief executive?"),
  documents = gr_example(),
  answers = list("45.2 million", NA),
  unanswerable = "ceo", split = "test")
arms <- gr_arms(c("fast", "thorough"))
bench <- hr_benchmark(arms, ref, runs = 5, client = cl, scorer = gr_scorer_answer())
